newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Prime sees GWN EBIT A$10m by 18 mths.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Prime sees GWN EBIT A$10m by 18 mths.

text.p: Prime Television Ltd said on Tuesday it expected to lift the earnings before interest and tax (EBIT) of the Golden West Network (GWN), which it bought earlier today, to about A$10 million in the next 12 to 18 months.
Prime's managing director, George Brown told reporters at a press conference that Prime believed GWN's operating earnings potential exceeded A$10 million a year.
Asked how long it would take Prime to lift GWN's earnings to that level, Brown said: "About 12 to 18 months."
Earlier today Prime said it bought GWN for A$71 million from Kerry Stokes' unlisted company Australian Capital Equity (ACE).
Prime said GWN had budgeted for revenues of A$30 million and earnings of A$7.2 million in the year to June 30, 1997.
"GWN is expecting to achieve a significant reduction in its satellite distribution costs through the introduction of digital compression technology in 1997," Brown said.
He said these changes were estimated to reduce GWN's operating costs by A$1 million a year.

"As part of the sale agreement between Prime Television and ACE, we will receive a warranty from the vendor in respect of the continued good standing of the programming agreement with the Nine Network," Brown said.

Earlier this year, monopolies watchdog, the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) commenced action seeking to overturn the long-term programming agreement entered into by GWN and Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd's Nine Network.
"GWN has indicated its intention to vigorously contest the action and this will not change as a result of the sale," Brown said.

He said that before deciding to purchase GWN, Prime's board had taken into account the fact that the Australian Broadcasting Authority (ABA) was assessing whether it should invite bids for a second regional television licence in Western Australia.
"The board believes that GWN will continue to generate significant profits even under a competitive environment," Brown said.
He said the price of A$71 million represented an earnings multiple of about seven times which he said was low in comparison to other recent buys in Australia's media sector.

"Prime continues to actively pursue acquisition opportunities in Australia and overseas," Brown said, adding that it had identified 23 countries where it could apply its skills in a rewarding fashion.
